contributions: Introduces R-GCN with relation-specific weight matrices and basis decomposition to control parameter explosion
Presents HAN with two-level hierarchical attention over manually specified meta-paths
Describes HGT with meta-relation-specific key/query/value projections for type-aware transformer attention
Demonstrates practical implementation of heterogeneous GNNs in PyTorch Geometric for node classification
limitations: R-GCN suffers from parameter explosion with many relation types unless basis decomposition is used
HAN requires manual meta-path specification, demanding domain knowledge and scaling poorly to graphs with many relation types
HAN materializes dense meta-path-expanded adjacency matrices, increasing memory usage
Heterogeneous GNNs must handle varying feature dimensions across node types and support inductive learning on large-scale graphs
methods: The chapter defines heterogeneous graphs formally and introduces meta-paths to capture composite semantic relationships. R-GCN applies separate weight matrices per relation type, using basis decomposition to reduce parameters. HAN expands meta-path-induced subgraphs and applies node-level attention within each meta-path and semantic-level attention across meta-paths. HGT extends multi-head transformer attention by parameterizing key, query, and value projections per meta-relation, with learned attention priors, allowing multi-hop type-aware propagation through layer stacking. All models use type-specific linear projections to map heterogeneous feature spaces into a shared embedding space.
results: For OGB-MAG with 4 meta-relations and dimension d=64, R-GCN uses 16,384 relation parameters per layer. For FB15k-237 (237 relations), basis decomposition with B=3 reduces parameters from ~970,752 to ~12,999 (a 74× reduction). HGT with 4 meta-relations, d=256, and 8 attention heads requires approximately 98,000 parameters per layer for type-specific weights. HAN's semantic attention is interpretable, with meta-path importance scores reflecting task relevance.
tldr: This chapter extends message passing to heterogeneous graphs via three architectures (R-GCN, HAN, HGT) that handle multiple node and edge types through relation-specific weights, meta-paths, type-specific projections, and attention mechanisms.
